Man I’m kinda stuck right now. No car, out here it’s like if you can’t drive you don’t exist. I been trying to pick up seasonal work but it’s all “gotta have reliable transportation” like I’m not trying.

I’m trying to stay sober too… mainly so I can see my kid more and not have my baby’s mom and the court thinking I’m just a screwup. I got a court thing coming up and it’s got me tight.

Real talk, what’s a simple day plan I can run that don’t cost money? Like stuff I can do when cravings hit and I’m just sitting there. And any ideas on job searching when you don’t got rides? I don’t wanna deal with “the system” more than I have to.

Hey AS, I hear how tough this feels—being stuck without a car and fighting to stay sober for your kid. That’s a lot, and I’m glad you’re reaching out. Let’s focus on a simple day plan to help with cravings and some job ideas.

For cravings, start your day with a quick walk if you can—fresh air helps clear your mind. When urges hit, try deep breathing for 5 minutes: inhale for 4, hold for 4, exhale for 4. Keep a small object, like a coin, to fidget with—it can ground you. Also, set a timer for a 10-minute distraction, like listening to a podcast or writing down why you’re staying sober. These are free and doable anywhere.

For jobs, look into remote or freelance gigs online—think data entry or customer service chats. Sites like Upwork or Indeed have filters for “work from home.” Also, check local spots within walking distance, like small stores or cafes; sometimes they’re flexible if you explain your situation.

I’m here if you want to talk more about the court stress or anything else. What’s one thing you’re feeling most stuck on right now?

Yeah… it’s like I’m doing the right stuff and still getting punished for not having a ride. I wake up and it’s just this heavy feeling, then my brain starts doing that “what’s the point” thing.

Can you lay out a day plan like hour-by-hour? Nothing fancy. Like morning, midday, night. I need it simple or I won’t follow it.

And when cravings hit it’s usually late afternoon, like 4-7, when I’m bored and everybody’s getting off work. What do I do in that exact window?

Also… I gotta text my kid’s mom without it turning into a fight. Just something short that don’t sound weak, but don’t start drama either. Real talk, can you help me write that?

Hey AS, I get that heavy “what’s the point” feeling—it’s rough. Let’s break your day into a simple structure to keep you grounded, plus tackle that late afternoon craving window and the text to your kid’s mom.

**Day Plan (Simple):**  
- **Morning (8-9 AM):** Get up, splash water on your face, eat something small if you can. Take a 10-minute walk or just step outside for air.  
- **Midday (12-1 PM):** Focus on one task—job search online or tidy a small space. Then, breathe deep for 5 minutes to reset.  
- **Night (8-9 PM):** Wind down with a free podcast or write a quick note about one good thing from the day.  

**Late Afternoon (4-7 PM) Cravings:** Keep busy—do push-ups or pace while listening to music. Call a friend or join a free online sobriety group (like SMART Recovery meetings). Chew gum or sip water to keep your hands and mouth occupied.

**Text to Kid’s Mom:** “Hey, just checking in about [kid’s name]. I’m working on things and want to be there more. Can we talk soon?” It’s direct, shows effort, no drama.

Which part feels hardest right now? I’m here.

- 8:00-8:20: Eat something cheap if you got it (toast, oats, eggs, whatever). Water.
- 8:20-8:45: Outside time. Walk to the end of the road and back, or just sit on the steps. No phone for 10 minutes.
- 9:00-10:00: Job stuff (one hour). If you don’t got internet, write a list of places within walking/bike distance and a plan to call.
- 10:00-10:15: Quick reset: shower or change clothes. It matters for your head.

Midday
- 12:00-12:30: Lunch / water.
- 12:30-1:00: One “grown-up” thing: paperwork, laundry, clean one corner, whatever. One thing.
- 1:00-2:00: Skill/earning block: online application, call a place, or watch a free YouTube on interview answers and write yours down.
- 2:00-3:30: Free time that’s not a trap: walk, stretch, music, library if you can get there, anything that’s not sitting and spiraling.

Late afternoon danger window (4-7) — exact play-by-play
- 3:45: Eat a snack + water. Seriously. Hungry + tired turns into cravings fast.
- 4:00-4:20: Move your body. Fast walk, stairs, pushups against the wall, whatever. Break a sweat a little.
- 4:20-4:30: Cold water on face or hold an ice cube. Sounds dumb but it snaps your brain out of that loop.
- 4:30-5:15: “Hands busy” task: dishes, sweep, fix something small, fold clothes, clean your phone photos, anything.
- 5:15-5:30: Text one safe person or post in a sober forum. Just: “Cravings right now. Checking in.”
- 5:30-6:15: Dinner / make food. Even basic.
- 6:15-7:00: Distraction you actually like: music + walk, game, podcast, YouTube. Timer on 20 minutes at a time so it doesn’t turn into doom-scrolling.

Night
- 8:00-8:30: Set up tomorrow: clothes out, list 3 tasks, charge phone.
- 9:00: Shower if you can, or wash face/brush teeth.
- 9:15-9:30: Write one line: “I stayed sober today because ____.” Keep it simple.
- 10:30-11:00: Try to lay down same time.

Job hunting with no ride (real talk options)
- Look for work you can walk to: gas station, grocery, dishwashing, stock, janitorial, warehouse, farm/seasonal crews that pick up at one spot.
- Ask about carpool straight up: “I don’t have a car right now but I’m reliable—anyone on your team come from my area?” Some places will.
- Remote stuff if you got a phone: customer support chat, surveys are weak money but can keep you busy, basic gig apps. Library Wi‑Fi if you can reach it.
- If there’s a church/community board, sometimes there’s cash jobs posted that don’t care about the ‘reliable transportation’ line as much.
